title: Design System: Ali Nojoumi, control plane

display.purpose: Company names on case covers, the Lab cover, and the contact statement.

hero.purpose: The one headline sentence; the name inside it is 700 and gold.

title.purpose: Sub-section headings; panel and tab names at 1.3125rem.

lead.purpose: The sentence under a heading, in mist, max 58ch.

label.purpose: Buttons, toggles, chips, row names. Sentence case.

note.purpose: Scope lines, legends, toy-model notes, in steel.

data.purpose: Process ids, states, counts, hashes, ledger rows, clock.

shadows.name: slab-cast
shadows.value: SVG parallelogram on the floor, fill #000 at 0.36, offset down-left by 0.5 + 0.45 x height
shadows.purpose: Cast shadow under every isometric slab. Drawn, never a CSS shadow.

shadows.name: lens
shadows.purpose: The glass lens over the portrait only.

shadows.name: packet-ring
shadows.purpose: Gold ring around the white packet on the rail.

shadows.name: hotspot-ring
shadows.purpose: Separates a hotspot dot from the photograph.

shadows.name: monogram-drop
shadows.purpose: The rendered titanium monogram resting on the gold field (filter).

shadows.name: hero-text
shadows.purpose: text-shadow that keeps hero copy legible over the portrait edge.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Page default, exponential ease-out (CSS --ease and ease.out).

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Closing and leaving: lens close, block hide, packet run.

motion.name: ease-soft
motion.purpose: Defined in the preset file as a softer ease-out.

motion.name: spring-counter
motion.purpose: Figures settling on the telemetry strip.

motion.name: spring-magnetic
motion.purpose: Buttons that lean toward the pointer.

motion.name: spring-panel
motion.purpose: Switch thumb, segmented thumb, slabs changing height or tone.

motion.name: swap
motion.purpose: Headline and process table trade places.

motion.name: packet
motion.purpose: A sample payment runs the rails.

motion.name: telemetry-glint
motion.purpose: Emerald light travelling along the top of the strip; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: hotspot-ping
motion.purpose: Ring pulsing around a hotspot; removed under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
The page is an architect's scale model of a financial system, seen at night. The floor is obsidian, etched with a fine square grid. One warm gold key light comes from the upper right, the same light that falls on the portraits and on every rendered cover. Systems are drawn as isometric slabs standing on that floor, joined by right-angle rails that carry light. Nothing floats in a card for decoration: a thing on this page is either part of the model, a control that operates it, or a readout from it.

Three devices make the world its own. The isometric model language draws every diagram from one small kit (slab, floor, rail, tag). The rail on the left edge maps the page as a vertical line with diamond nodes, and a white packet rides it with the scroll. The lens is a circle of glass that rests on the portrait and shows a second photograph through it; a switch grows it over the whole portrait. The page is dark from the first pixel to the last section, and then ends on one flat field of gold.

The density is that of an instrument panel read by an executive: large Syne statements, plain Inter explanation, and small mono readouts where a machine would speak. Surfaces are flat. Depth belongs to the model and to the photographs.
keyCharacteristics: Obsidian floor with a 64px etched grid at 4% steel, behind everything.
One light direction, upper right, in the photographs, the hero wash, the slab faces and the cast shadows.
Isometric slabs and right-angle light rails for every diagram, on their own opaque floor.
A fixed 76px rail with diamond nodes and a travelling packet on desktop; a 60px glass bar on phones.
A glass lens over the portrait as the signature interaction.
Four signal colours with fixed meanings: gold, emerald, cyan, steel.
Square corners (0 on panels, 2px on controls); pills only for the skill filters.
One flat gold field, used once, for contact.

rules.name: The Four Signals Rule
rules.body: Gold is the person and what he does. Emerald is money moving and approval. Cyan is simulation data. Steel is structure. A colour never borrows another's meaning, and none of the three signals is used as decoration.

rules.name: The One Gold Field Rule
rules.body: Gold floods exactly one surface, the contact section, where the palette inverts to obsidian text and obsidian buttons on flat gold. Everywhere else gold is a mark: a word, a button, a node, a rim.

rules.name: The Upper Right Rule
rules.body: Light comes from the upper right in every image, wash, slab and shadow. The hero wash is a gold radial at 17% anchored to the top right corner; shadows fall down and to the left.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for what a machine would print: identifiers, figures, states, counts, hashes, ledger rows, the clock. Headings, sentences and button labels are never mono.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All interface text is sentence case with no added letter-spacing. Hierarchy comes from face, size and weight. A heading stands alone with its lead; nothing small sits above it.

rules.name: The Negative Track Rule
rules.body: Syne is always tracked in (-0.015em at title size to -0.04em at display size) and set at a line-height near 1. Inter is never tracked.

rules.name: The Rail Rule
rules.body: On desktop the page is navigated by the rail and nothing else: a monogram at the top, a 1px line with one diamond node per section, a gold fill and a white packet that follow the scroll, and a gold email button at the foot. There is no top navigation bar on desktop.

rules.name: The Drawn Depth Rule
rules.body: Panels, buttons and cards carry no box-shadow at rest or on hover. If something needs to look raised, it is drawn as a slab in the model with its cast shadow, or it is glass over a photograph.

rules.name: The Glass Needs A Subject Rule
rules.body: A blurred translucent surface is used only where there is an image or moving content behind it to blur. Over the plain floor, a surface is opaque carbon.

rules.name: The Diamond Rule
rules.body: A position in a sequence is marked with a 45 degree diamond, never a numbered circle or a bullet.

dos: Do keep the obsidian floor and its 64px grid behind every dark section, and keep the light in the upper right.
Do draw any new diagram with the kit in `src/lib/iso.ts` and `src/components/ui.tsx`: slabs on an opaque floor, right-angle rails, tags with an obsidian halo.
Do give each colour its one meaning: gold for the person and his actions, emerald for money moving and approval, cyan for simulation data, steel for structure.
Do use JetBrains Mono for machine output (ids, figures, states, hashes) and Inter for everything a person says.
Do keep corners square: 0 on panels, 2px on controls.
Do mark steps and positions with 45 degree diamonds.
Do state the scope and date under every figure, in steel, and label every toy model as a toy in a note beside it.
Do keep a 2px gold focus outline (obsidian on the gold field) on every interactive element, including slabs.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion state with all content present.
donts: Don't put a box-shadow on a panel, card or button. Cast shadows belong to slabs, the lens and the monogram.
Don't use gold as a background anywhere except the contact field, or use emerald or cyan as decoration.
Don't add a pill anywhere but the skill filters, or round a panel.
Don't set headings, sentences or button labels in mono, or set interface text in tracked capitals.
Don't draw a system as flat boxes and arrows, a node graph, or a chart. If it is a system, it is a model on the floor.
Don't frame the portrait or place it in a card. It stands on the stage and feathers into the floor.
Don't use glass over the plain floor; blur only where a photograph or moving content sits behind.
Don't let a spring bounce or a transition ease in slowly. Things settle.
Don't borrow the sibling steel-watch site's furniture (dials, bezels, tick rings, gauge arcs). This world draws with slabs, rails and a lens; the watch appears only on his wrist in the photographs.
Don't add a top navigation bar on desktop. The rail is the navigation.
